clue.text: One getting some kicks as a communist?

definitions.meaning: a footballer who plays out on the left flank, taking his share of kicks
a communist is someone on the far left of politics

explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link joining the two senses; the surface suggests a thrill-seeking revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a left-flank football player and a radical of the political left go by this hyphenated name.

clue.text: Own a pledge

parts.note: a pledge is a solemn promise, a vow

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to make a personal promise.
explanation.definitionFit: To own a fact is to admit or declare it openly, a synonym.

clue.text: Sound of bouncer being punched by unknown with phone, in fight scene?

indicators.note: the punch drives one piece into the middle of the other, so the sound is broken open

parts.note: boing is the noise of something springy bouncing
X is the classic algebraic unknown
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman gets hit by a stranger holding a mobile during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman and 'punched' a fight, but the bouncer is anything springy and the punch is just an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The roped square where boxers fight is literally the scene of a fight, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sweet kid

definitions.meaning: to kid someone is to trick or tease them

explanation.definitionFit: The cold dessert and the verb meaning to deceive share one spelling.

clue.text: Current interest in western shows, dubious

indicators.note: something dubious is not straight, so these letters are not to be taken in their printed order

explanation.surface: Cowboy films are suspected of being popular right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like part of a phrase about electricity; here it means topical, and 'dubious' at the end is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being worth reporting is what makes a story of topical public interest.

clue.text: North America abandoned true quality

indicators.note: abandoned in the sense of wild or uninhibited, so the letters run loose

explanation.surface: A continent is said to have given up on honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks as though it removes North America from something, but it signals a rearrangement of the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing's essential character or innate quality is its nature.

clue.text: Principal clergyman behind revolutionary papers

indicators.note: behind places the clergyman after the reversed papers
a revolution turns something round, so the word for papers is read backwards

parts.note: ID, identity papers
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A senior vicar stands behind some radical documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A school principal or head of an organisation is called its director.

clue.text: Western god in Eastern dynasty — it's a plant!

indicators.note: in places the western god inside the name of the dynasty

parts.note: the Han dynasty ruled China
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: An exclamation reveals that a Western deity in a Chinese dynasty is actually vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Han dynasty ruled China from 206 BC; 'in' opens it up for the western god.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorny shrub of hedgerows, also called may, is a plant.

clue.text: Opera's mechanics?

parts.note: read as the men who fix cars, this Bizet opera's title splits into two plain words

explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to ask about stagecraft, but the title of Bizet's opera, read as two words, describes motor mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's opera about a Seville gypsy splits into words naming men who work on cars.

clue.text: Firm — as are broccoli, pecorino and butterscotch?

definitions.meaning: a firm owning shares in other firms

definitions.text: as are broccoli, pecorino and butterscotch?
definitions.meaning: each of these three words contains the letters CO, the abbreviation for company

explanation.walkthrough: CO is short for company; broCColi, peCOrino and butterSCOTch each hold a CO, so each is literally holding company.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm whose business is owning controlling stakes in other businesses is a parent corporation of this kind.

clue.text: Some larkspur, a lovely flower

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gardener admires some pretty larkspur in bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' suggests a bloom, matching larkspur, but it means something that flows: the Ural is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a flower in the crossword sense of something that flows, and the Ural is a Russian river.

clue.text: Aggressive force — one beginning to unleash any bombs

indicators.note: the pieces are blown apart and reassembled, like debris after explosions

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the first letter only of unleash is taken

explanation.surface: A warning that a military power is about to drop its bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: FORCE, I, U and ANY are shuffled together; 'bombs' is the anagram signal, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Confrontational, blatantly assertive behaviour is described by this colloquial phrase.

clue.text: Big cheese, foremost of camemberts taken with water in West Country

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England

indicators.note: foremost picks just the opening letter of camemberts

explanation.surface: A cheese-lover eats camembert beside a river in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England; its River Exe flows through Exeter.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is an important person, as is a business executive, shortened to this.

clue.text: Red Army ordered tipple

parts.note: blood is red, so red can stand for bloody

indicators.note: the letters of army are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Soviet soldiers place an order for drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Army' reads as one phrase, but RED gives BLOODY and only ARMY is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of vodka and tomato juice is a well-known alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Send up old US wolf

parts.note: to lob is to send something high into the air

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an ageing American wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send up' looks like a reversal, but it is LOB, a high throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A timber wolf of the south-western United States and Mexico is known by this Spanish name.

clue.text: Beast gatecrashing brief celebration is most ravishing

indicators.note: a gatecrasher forces a way inside, so the beast goes into the party
brief means cut short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a fiesta is a festive celebration
an ox is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: An animal crashes a short party and turns out to be the most gorgeous guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' drops the last letter of the celebration word before the beast crashes in; foxy is slang for sexy.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxy means sexually attractive, so the superlative is the most alluring.

clue.text: Seat turns on monster locks

parts.note: to turn a handle or road is to wind
an orc is a monster of fantasy fiction
locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A rotating seat is fitted onto a hairy monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; the surface makes 'turns on' sound like rotating.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden chair with a spindle back, named after an English town, is a type of seat.

clue.text: Fine discussion's ultimate quarrel

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so the last letter of discussion is picked

parts.note: a quarrel is a bolt shot from a crossbow, a kind of arrow

explanation.surface: A debate's final point turns into an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' wants to mean argument; it is the archer's bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine in the sense of thin or slender, as a fine line, is a synonym.

clue.text: Clever chap finding last of ale in mug

indicators.note: the final letter of ale is the one taken

parts.note: a stein is a large beer mug

explanation.surface: A clever man finds the dregs of his beer in a tankard.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist's name is used generically for any genius, especially ironically.

clue.text: Merciless sun's ending in the shade

indicators.note: in puts the final letter inside the colour

parts.note: violet is a shade of colour

indicators.note: ending selects the last letter of sun

explanation.surface: A pitiless sun sets in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' suggests shadow out of the sun, but means a colour; N goes into VIOLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent can mean savage and without restraint, close in sense to cruel.

clue.text: Thriving, bound to be a source of abundant supply

parts.note: to be well is to be in good health, thriving
a bound is a leap, a spring

explanation.surface: A flourishing enterprise is certain to keep supplying plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to be' reads as 'certain to be'; 'bound' is a leap and 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fountainhead is figuratively an inexhaustible origin, the main meaning of this word.

clue.text: Asquith's lot reliably unsure about role

indicators.note: about means around, so the anagram goes round the role
being unsure of a word's letters, they are set out differently

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Someone is not confident about their job.
explanation.walkthrough: H H Asquith was a British prime minister (1908-16). 'unsure' scrambles the adverb, and 'about' wraps the result round the role.
explanation.definitionFit: Asquith led this British political group, so his lot means his party.

clue.text: Free, like a TV aerial?

definitions.meaning: a drink given at no charge is provided by the establishment
a television aerial is mounted up on a building's roof

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means given at no cost by the establishment, and literally describes something on a building.

clue.text: Nothing to withdraw from loan, current cheque bouncing first

indicators.note: a bouncing cheque comes back, so the whole string is read backwards
withdrawing takes the letter out of the word that follows

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
I is the symbol for electric current
a giro is a British state benefit cheque

explanation.surface: A loan is cancelled after the first cheque bounced.
explanation.walkthrough: LOAN without O is LAN; LAN + I + GIRO read backwards gives the answer. A giro is a UK benefit payment cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: Original means first in time, the earliest version before copies.

clue.text: Scottish hero, champion of partition?

parts.note: a wall is a dividing partition
an ace is a top performer, a champion

explanation.surface: A Scottish patriot also proved a champion of dividing walls.
explanation.walkthrough: William Wallace led Scottish resistance against England in the 1290s.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wallace led the Scots against Edward I and is a national hero of Scotland.

clue.text: Body briefly set up to incorporate new state

indicators.note: incorporate means take into the body, so one piece goes inside
in a down clue, set up means written upwards, reversed
briefly means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: anatomy can mean the body

explanation.surface: A newly established organisation is briefly set up to absorb a new country.
explanation.walkthrough: ANATOMY shortened to ANATOM is turned round by 'set up' to MOTANA, then 'to incorporate' takes in N.
explanation.definitionFit: Montana is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Native Australian houses lean not entirely in French style

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the Australian animal wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a roo, kangaroo, is a native of Australia

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to cock something is to tilt or lean it

explanation.surface: Aboriginal homes are only partly built in a French manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native Australian' suggests a person but is the kangaroo; 'not entirely' cuts the last letter from the word for lean before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo was an ornate decorative style that arose in 18th-century France.

clue.text: Really precise

definitions.meaning: an intensifier meaning truly or extremely
exact, as in the exact spot

explanation.definitionFit: The word means extremely as an adverb and exact, as in the very spot, as an adjective.
